title: `percentile_cont` and `median` interpolate linearly; `percentile_disc` takes the lower value, as a double
verdict: `quantile_interp`: `cont` linear at (n - 1)·p; `disc` the value at ⌈n·p⌉, returned as `DOUBLE`
description: `median`, `percentile(x, p)` and `percentile_cont(p) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x)` interpolate linearly at position (n - 1)·p: over 1, 2, 3, 10 the median is 2.5 and `p = 0.25` 1.75. `percentile_disc(p)` takes the first value whose cumulative share reaches p (1 at 0.25, 2 at 0.26 over 1, 2, 3, 4). All three return `DOUBLE`, for integer and decimal inputs too (`median` of two `DECIMAL(10,2)` is 1.675 as a double). `percentile_approx` is approximate and returns the input type.
NULLs are skipped; NaN sorts last (spark-nan-order). The fraction must be a constant.
reference: `quantile_disc` takes a value of the input, of its type; `quantile_cont` any double between the neighbours (`contAllowed`). Spark's positions match; `percentile_disc` of integers and decimals needs a cast back to the input type, exact for integers below 2⁵³.

evidence.note: `getPercentile`: position (n - 1)·p, floor and ceil, linear interpolation unless `discrete`

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
